question: Your extraction system reads supplier invoices and calls a vendor lookup tool with the extracted vendor name to add a vendor ID to each JSON record. All records pass schema validation, but audits find that some invoices carry the wrong vendor ID. Logs show that in each failed case the lookup returned two or more vendors with the same name. The system prompt tells the agent to always fill the vendor ID with the closest match. What is the most likely root cause of the wrong vendor IDs?

options.text: Lost-in-the-middle effects in long invoices cause the agent to miss the vendor name before it calls the lookup.
options.reason: The agent extracted the vendor name, and the lookup returned records with that name. The error comes from choosing among several matches, not from missing information in the context.

options.text: The JSON schema runs without strict mode, so malformed vendor ID values slip past validation into downstream systems.
options.reason: Strict mode eliminates syntax errors. Here the IDs are well formed and pass validation, but they belong to the wrong vendor because the agent guessed among matches.

options.text: The system prompt makes the agent choose among multiple matches by heuristic instead of asking for an additional identifier.
options.reason: When a lookup returns multiple matches, the agent should request additional identifiers. The 'closest match' instruction forces a heuristic guess, which produces wrong but valid IDs.

options.text: The vendor lookup tool has a minimal description, so the agent calls it in place of a more suitable tool.
options.reason: Weak descriptions cause tool misselection. Here the logs show that the right tool was called and returned several valid matches, so tool selection is not the failure.
